Death of Basil of Caesarea (traditional date).
Pope Leo X excommunicates Martin Luther (Decet Romanum Pontificem).
Pope Paul VI and Patriarch Athenagoras I meet in Jerusalem, the first such meeting in centuries.
Epiphany: the manifestation of Christ, and in the East his baptism.
The Orthodox Church of Ukraine receives its tomos of autocephaly from Constantinople.
Death of Antony of Egypt, father of monks (traditional date).
First adult (believer’s) baptisms in Zurich: the birth of the Anabaptist movement.
Emperor Henry IV begins three days of penance in the snow at Canossa.
Pope John XXIII announces his plan for an ecumenical council (Vatican II).
Death of Henry VIII of England.
Bernadette Soubirous reports her first vision at Lourdes.
Pope Benedict XVI announces his resignation.
Pope Francis and Patriarch Kirill of Moscow meet in Havana.
Death in Rome of Constantine-Cyril, apostle of the Slavs.
Death of Martin Luther at Eisleben.
Martyrdom of Polycarp of Smyrna (traditional date; the year may be 156).
Diocletian’s soldiers destroy the church at Nicomedia; the Great Persecution begins.
Swiss Anabaptists adopt the Schleitheim Confession.
Martyrdom of Perpetua and Felicity at Carthage (traditional date).
Constantine makes Sunday a public day of rest.
The ‘Triumph of Orthodoxy’: icons restored in Constantinople, ending Iconoclasm.
Death of Pope Gregory the Great.
Jorge Mario Bergoglio is elected Pope Francis.
Death of Benedict of Nursia (traditional date).
Thomas Cranmer is burned at Oxford.
Archbishop Óscar Romero is shot while celebrating Mass in San Salvador.
The Annunciation: Gabriel’s message to Mary.
Ferdinand and Isabella sign the decree expelling the Jews from Spain.
Death of Pope John Paul II.
Prayer meetings in Los Angeles begin the Azusa Street revival.
Dietrich Bonhoeffer is executed at Flossenbürg.
Luther refuses to recant before the Diet of Worms.
Death of Pope Francis on Easter Monday.
Galerius’ edict of toleration is published at Nicomedia.
The Second Council of Constantinople opens.
Robert Francis Prevost is elected Pope Leo XIV.
The Council of Nicaea opens (traditional date).
John Wesley feels his heart ‘strangely warmed’ at Aldersgate Street.
Death of John Calvin in Geneva.
Constantinople falls to the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II.
The Confessing Church adopts the Barmen Declaration.
Licinius’ letter granting toleration (the ‘Edict of Milan’) is posted at Nicomedia.
The World Missionary Conference opens at Edinburgh.
The Creed of Nicaea is adopted (traditional date).
At Ephesus, Cyril’s council deposes Nestorius.
Galileo abjures before the Roman Inquisition.
The Augsburg Confession is presented to Charles V.
Feast of Saints Peter and Paul.
Jan Hus is burned at the Council of Constance.
The Council of Florence proclaims union of the Greek and Latin churches (Laetentur caeli).
The First Council of Constantinople closes.
Papal legates lay a bull of excommunication on the altar of Hagia Sophia.
The Great Fire of Rome begins; Nero blames the Christians.
Vatican I defines papal infallibility (Pastor aeternus).
The ‘Robber Synod’ (Second Council of Ephesus) opens.
Edith Stein (Teresa Benedicta of the Cross) is murdered at Auschwitz.
Death in exile of Maximus the Confessor.
The Dormition (East) and Assumption (West) of Mary.
The World Council of Churches is founded at Amsterdam.
The Visigoths sack Rome; Augustine begins to think about The City of God.
The St Bartholomew’s Day massacre begins in Paris.
Death of Augustine at Hippo, during the Vandal siege.
Gregory the Great is consecrated bishop of Rome.
Death in exile of John Chrysostom.
The Second Council of Nicaea opens.
The Peace of Augsburg: cuius regio, eius religio.
Pope Paul III approves the Society of Jesus.
Death of Jerome at Bethlehem (traditional date).
Huldrych Zwingli is killed at the battle of Kappel.
Karol Wojtyła is elected Pope John Paul II.
The Peace of Westphalia ends the Thirty Years’ War.
Constantine defeats Maxentius at the Milvian Bridge.
Luther sends his Ninety-five Theses on indulgences.
Lutherans and Catholics sign the Joint Declaration on Justification.
Pope Pius XII defines the Assumption of Mary.
The Third Council of Constantinople opens.
Death of Pope Leo the Great.
Martin V is elected at Constance, ending the Western Schism.
Boniface VIII issues the bull Unam sanctam.
Vatican II promulgates Lumen gentium and the Decree on Ecumenism.
Urban II preaches the crusade at Clermont.
Rome and Constantinople lift the excommunications of 1054.
Pius IX defines the Immaculate Conception.
Luther burns the papal bull threatening him with excommunication.
Traditional date of the apparition of Our Lady of Guadalupe.
Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne emperor in St Peter’s.
